newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan minister says Clinton funding impossible.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan minister says Clinton funding impossible.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign minister said on Thursday he believed the island's ruling party did not make illegal contributions to U.S. President Bill Clinton's election campaign, and Taipei would be cleared of any wrongdoing.

The Chinese-language edition of Asiaweek magazine had last week quoted Liu Tai-ying, chairman of the ruling Nationalist Party's business management committee, as expressing a willingness to donate US$15 million to the Clinton campaign.

"This is something that is impossible according to logic," Foreign Minister John Chang said on state television when asked about the donation. "It is impossible to donate such a large sum without having anyone know about it."
The Nationalist Party on Tuesday denied making the contribution.

Reports of illegal campaign contribution from foreign forces have fuelled partisan mud-slinging in the final week before the U.S. election, with Republican challenger Bob Dole using the issue to assail Clinton's character.
When asked about a reported meeting between Clinton and Liu, Chang said he did not know of such an encounter but would not be disturbed if it had taken place.
"It would be a pity if our government did not have some help from private forces (to further foreign relations)," Chang said.
The U.S. officially recognises China and does not have formal diplomatic ties with Taiwan.

Earlier this week, the U.S. magazine Newsweek quoted Taiwan officials as saying local firms had complained of being pressured to contribute to the Clinton campaign by James Wood, chairman of Washington's de facto embassy in Taipei.
Wood denied the charge to Newsweek.
Chang said any contact between Wood and Taiwan business leaders would be private in nature and did not represent either government.
"I am confident our government will not become a scapegoat of the reports on illegal campaign contributions. The U.S. government will evaluate the issue very objectively," he said.

The Nationalist Party, which ruled China until its defeat by the communists in 1949 and fled into exile on Taiwan, is one of the world's richest political organisations with T$37.8 billion (US$1.4 billion) in assets under seven holding companies.
